title: DependencyMapperItems
description: Shape of content.items for L1-planning-dependency-mapper. DELIBERATE, REASONED DEPARTURE from the Items+Artifacts Meta-Points Pattern used by every other document-producing agent in this framework. That pattern exists to separate a long-form NARRATIVE a human reads (the artifact, full text) from condensed summary/*_summary meta-points a downstream agent can reconcile against programmatically (items). A dependency graph has no narrative to condense away from in the first place: nodes[], edges[], cycle_check, and critical_path are already maximally structured, machine-consumed data — writing a 'summary' of a graph would just be the same graph with its fields renamed, not a genuine compression. So items here carries the EXACT SAME content as the artifact, field for field, not a condensation of it — items and the artifact are the same content, unlike every other agent in this framework. The artifact (dependency-graph.json) still exists and is still saved to s3, per this framework's storage convention, so L1-planning-backlog-prioritizer (topological-sort input) and Phase 4's L1-design-hld can retrieve the raw JSON file directly without unwrapping an AgentOutput envelope. Structure is adapted DIRECTLY from phase-1/templates/dependency-graph.template.json's own JSON Schema — that template already IS the correct shape for this agent's output; there is no prose template requiring S4 embedding. One further departure from the framework's usual 'every item carries confidence + reasoning' rule (see agent-creator.md Key Pattern #1): nodes and edges carry none, by design — a graph edge's correctness is not a self-assessed confidence judgment, it is a fact independently verifiable by DFS traversal (cycle_check) and longest-path computation (critical_path). Those two fields ARE this agent's confidence-equivalent: a PASS/FAIL and a rationale earned by actually running the algorithm, not asserted.

type.description: component = new/existing system to be built; external-dependency = a real prerequisite outside the build (partner, vendor, unselected methodology) — not the same as an org-internal existing system already covered in impact-assessment.md's Existing-System Impact section

source_requirement.description: All FR-NNN ids this node traces back to, from prd.md — required for every component node (external-dependency nodes have no FR of their own, they gate one). A node satisfying multiple requirements (e.g. one reporting component covering two metrics) must list all of them, not just the first. Every FR in prd.md must appear in some node's source_requirement across the whole graph — a requirement with no covering node is a dropped requirement, not a rounding error.

from.description: node id — ALWAYS the upstream/prerequisite node, regardless of edge type

to.description: node id — ALWAYS the downstream/dependent node, regardless of edge type

type.description: Direction is UNIFORM across all three types: 'from' must exist/complete before 'to' can proceed. depends-on = hard technical prerequisite between two components; blocks = an external-dependency node gating a component; integrates-with = non-blocking peer integration (failure of 'to' does not halt 'from'). Never mix directions within or across types — every edge follows prerequisite -> dependent so a single consistent forward DFS/topological walk works for cycle_check and critical_path both. A schema validator cannot detect a reversed edge (both orderings are syntactically valid); this is caught only by re-running the traversal and checking the resulting critical_path makes sense against impact-assessment.md's own stated blast-radius/prerequisite narrative.

status.description: Result of an ACTUAL depth-first-search traversal over every node/edge, walking recursion-stack membership to detect a back-edge — never asserted from 'the graph looks acyclic'. FAIL means a genuine cycle exists and this agent's own overall AgentOutput status must be 'failed' (escalate to HITL), never silently resolved by dropping an edge.

cycles_found.description: Empty array if status is PASS. If status is FAIL, each inner array is the exact node-id sequence (in traversal order, repeating the start node at the end) forming one detected cycle — not a paraphrase of 'there is a cycle somewhere'.

nodes.description: Ordered node ids forming the longest BLOCKING chain, computed by an actual longest-path traversal over depends-on/blocks edges only — integrates-with edges are excluded from this computation entirely since they are non-blocking by definition. Empty array only if cycle_check.status is FAIL and a valid longest path cannot yet be computed pending cycle resolution.

rationale.description: Must state the computed path length (edge count) and name any other chain that is exactly as long — a genuine TIE must be reported honestly as a tie (e.g. two independent root nodes converging on the same downstream node and sharing its entire tail), never arbitrarily resolved to a single 'winner'. If cycle_check.status is FAIL, this field explains why critical_path.nodes is empty and that computation is blocked pending cycle resolution, not silently skipped.
